newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses slide as Wall Street flounders.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses slide as Wall Street flounders.

text.p: European bourses, nervous all day of what might happen on Wall Street, slid further on Thursday afternoon as U.S. stocks made an indecisive start and then dived half a percent.

Leading London shares increased their losses after the New York start and German shares had already ended floor trading three-quarters of a percent lower. The Paris bourse, which had been mixed for most of the day, managed to remain positive but only just.
On the foreign exchange markets the dollar suffered in earlyean trade as the mark extended this week's gradual recovery.
But by the afternoon it was holding at around 1.5230 marks, above what analysts described as important support levels. Against the yen it was just under 33-month highs at around 112.90.
The mark's rise against so-called other European currencies like the lira and the Swedish crown was a central feature of the session, traders said.

Italy and Sweden cut their interest rates on Wednesday night and Thursday morning respectively but the Bundesbank's policy-making council, which met on Thursday, left German rates unchanged as expected.
The Swedish crown eased slightly in reaction to the the cut -- the 23rd this year -- but recovered after the Riksbank said further scope for easing was limited.

The lira also staged a recovery after dipping to 1007.00 against the mark in early trading, compared with 1003.10 in late Europe on Wednesday. Analysts said the lira's fall was exaggerated, given the good background news for Italian bonds, and by 1430 GMT it was trading at around 1003.75 to the mark.
Worries that markets on both sides of the Atlantic could be due for a major correction after their recent strong run had increased after Wall Street's third loss in a row overnight.
After trading lower early on, leading London stocks slipped further in the afternoon to lose more than half a percent after the New York open.

They had been boosted in early trading by a hike in value of chemicals giant ICI, which gained after its third-quarter profits, while lower, contained no new shocks for the stock market. Dealers said the market had also been underpinned by steady government bonds and a firm overnight performance from Treasuries.
ICI dominated early dealing, confounding market expectations with a 20-1/2 pence rise to 796, though it had slipped to 793 by mid-afternoon.
German shares ended the bourse session lower before Wall Street's opening, extending losses slightly after the Bundesbank said it had left its key rates unchanged.
The 30-share DAX index closes down 21.10 at 2,678.43.
French shares, which had been trading mixed all day, were just positive by mid-afternoon after a bout of profit-taking on the last day of the October account.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5230 marks and 112.90 yen compared with 1.5225 and 113.05 yen on Wednesday.
STOCKS AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was down 23.8 points at 4004.6.
Germany's DAX index closed down 21.1 at 2678.43.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 2.76 at 2,151.62.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed weaker at $383.00 compared with $383.55 at the close in London on Wednesday. Silver was lower with gold, down six cents at $4.92.
